levels.mesh_gate_failure: non-orthogonality 74.96 deg exceeds the lab's 70 deg gate (geometry_study.MAX_NON_ORTHOGONALITY)

numerical.method: 3-rung ladder (263,359 / 645,251 / 1,849,113 cells), all with resolved boundary layers (add_layers=True, target y+ 30). Cd and Cl are NOT monotonic across the ladder, so no Richardson extrapolation or observed-order fit is performed -- fitting an order to non-asymptotic data would manufacture false precision.
numerical.why_not_conclusive: medium->fine Cd fell 25% (0.024478->0.018262); fine->finer Cd moved <1% (0.018262->0.018327) but Cl swung back up 19% (0.209547->0.250179). The finer (largest, 1,849,113-cell) rung independently failed the lab's own mesh non-orthogonality gate (74.96 deg vs a 70 deg gate) and achieved only 58.3% of its target boundary-layer thickness (vs ~94% on the other two rungs), so its apparent near-plateau in Cd is not trusted as evidence of grid convergence.
numerical.graded_rung: fine (645,251 cells) -- the only rung passing both mesh-quality gates with full layer coverage

band_used_in_reference.note: the reference derivation (sdk/scripts/derive_naca4412_reference.py) folds this ladder's own Cd/Cl spread into its acceptance band as a direct numerical-uncertainty term, rather than computing an observed order.

superseded.reason: 2026-07-27: this earlier ladder had addLayers false at Re 1e6 (no boundary-layer cells at all) and archived no polyMesh, so it was not reproducible. Replaced by the layered ladder above (levels[]).

numerical.method: 3-mesh study (r = 1.35), observed order p = 4.62; least-squares fit with safety factor 1.25 (Eca and Hoekstra 2014); observed order limited to the theoretical range (band uses p = 2.5)
